title: Harden ordinary client pagination and recovery behavior
objective: Clients recover from expected source/generation limits without guessing.
outcome: A cursor for one tool/query cannot page a different collection. An expired cursor never silently begins a new generation. An unknown schema is not returned as an empty list of variables or a transport success claiming the task completed. Cancellation stops the current request. Clients neither retry nonretryable states nor lose the next-cursor/omitted-section explanation. Recovery behavior is documented with runnable examples. No acceptance check depends solely on status 200. A successful tool envelope is not a completed research task. worker/index.mjs does not import enrichment. Last-good generation live-2026-09-03-85b50522b420 is unchanged.

commits.subject: Unify cursor and generation guidance
commits.instructions: Map expired, malformed and wrong-generation cursors to precise restart instructions that preserve the research question and disclose snapshot change.
commits.verification: A cursor for one tool/query cannot page a different collection; an expired cursor never silently begins a new generation.

commits.subject: Preserve typed domain results
commits.instructions: Keep partial, unknown, empty, unavailable and blocked separate through HTTP/client envelopes. Align retryable flags and corrective actions.
commits.verification: An unknown schema is not returned as an empty list of variables or a transport success claiming the task completed.

commits.subject: Verify cancellation and output limits
commits.instructions: Exercise cancellation, slow responses, bounded collection output and oversize handling through the real client transport fixtures.
commits.verification: Cancellation stops the current request; clients neither retry nonretryable states nor lose the next-cursor/omitted-section explanation.
